title: Probability, statistics and information theory for machine learning
stage: College AI and machine learning degree
audience: a college student in an artificial intelligence, machine learning or computer science degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn the probabilistic toolkit of machine learning: joint, marginal and conditional distributions in several variables, covariance and the multivariate Gaussian, maximum likelihood and maximum a posteriori estimation, Bayesian inference with conjugate priors, sampling methods including importance sampling and Markov chain Monte Carlo, entropy, cross-entropy, KL divergence and mutual information, and the statistics of comparing models: bootstrap intervals and paired tests.
primary_reading: Information Theory, Inference, and Learning Algorithms by David MacKay (free PDF)

weeks.2: Expectation, covariance and the multivariate Gaussian
weeks.4: Maximum a posteriori estimation and regularization
weeks.8: Markov chain Monte Carlo: the Metropolis algorithm
weeks.11: The bootstrap and confidence intervals for model performance
weeks.12: Comparing models: paired tests and multiple comparisons

blocks.deliverable: Compute marginals and conditionals of a small joint table and of a two-dimensional Gaussian.
Derive the maximum-likelihood and MAP estimates for three models.
Update a Beta prior with data and report the posterior predictive probability.
Week 7 midterm; estimate an expectation by importance sampling.
Compute entropies and divergences and connect them to loss functions.
Report a bootstrap interval for the accuracy of a classifier.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Bayesian A/B analysis: for a supplied data set of outcomes from two model variants, compute maximum-likelihood and Bayesian estimates with Beta priors, simulate the posterior to estimate the probability that one variant is better, compute a bootstrap interval for the difference, and write a two-page report explaining the results and the assumptions behind them.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
